title: Claim-source verification annotation record (pilot, v0.1.0)
description: One record = one Wikipedia claim checked against its cited source(s). A record holds the claim, its sub-claims, the sources, and one or more assessments (original human, independent human review, or AI-generated). Fields listed under 'required' must be present, but most can be null or 'needs_review' so missing information is recorded honestly instead of invented.

claim_id.description: Required. The claim's label in the original report, for example 'A01'.

provenance.description: Optional. Where the information came from, so every field can be traced back.

source_document.description: File name or title of the report this record was converted from.

article.description: Required. The Wikipedia article containing the claim.

revision_id.description: Wikipedia revision the claim was taken from. null = not recorded.

claim.description: Required. The claim as it appears in Wikipedia.

text.description: Original wording or an explicitly labeled public summary.

text_status.description: 'public_summary' identifies a release paraphrase of the original claim.

location_in_article.description: Optional. Section and paragraph of the claim in the article.

paragraph_context.description: Optional. The surrounding paragraph, needed for paragraph-level context.

sub_claims.description: Required. At least one. A claim that is not split has exactly one sub-claim whose text equals the claim.

text.description: Claim fragment or whole claim if unsplit. Public summaries use corresponding paraphrases.

sources.description: Required. The cited source(s) the claim is checked against.

access.description: How the source could be reached. Describes access only; it is not a verdict.

note.description: What was tried and how the source was reached, in the assessor's words.

assessments.description: Required. One entry per assessor (and per context level if the same assessor repeats the check). Original human, independent human review and AI-generated assessments are told apart by 'kind'.

adjudication.description: Required. How the human reference for this record was settled. Disagreement is kept visible, never averaged away.

reference_label.description: The label used as the human reference. null = none yet.

reference_assessment_ids.description: Human assessments the reference is based on. AI assessments must never be listed (checked by the validation script).

needs_review_items.description: Required (may be empty). Everything the record's owner must still decide or fill in.

field.description: Path of the field, for example 'assessments[0].confidence'.

id.description: Stable lowercase identifier. Never reused or renumbered.

urlOrNull.description: Web address, or null if not recorded. Never guessed.

dateOrNull.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or null if not recorded.

verdictLabel.description: Five support verdicts plus needs_review, a workflow sentinel excluded from scoring.

location.description: Where the passage is in the source. null = that level was not recorded.

raw.description: The location exactly as originally written.

role.description: 'decisive' = the smallest passage that settles the verdict; 'nearest_topical' = closest passage when nothing supports the claim.

passage_text.description: Verbatim source quote when included. Null when unavailable or withheld from the public snapshot.

kind.description: Who produced this assessment. Keeps the three types distinguishable.

id.description: Pseudonymous stable id, or 'needs_review' if not yet decided.

product.description: AI only. The assistant's product name.

model_as_recorded.description: AI only. Model name exactly as written in the report. Not guessed.

context_level.description: Widest Wikipedia context actually used. Wider-world truth is NOT a level; use outside_knowledge_note.

assessability.description: Could the claim be assessed at all? This is separate from the verdict.

note.description: What was tried, and what was missing.

label.description: Standard label. Must be null when the claim could not be assessed.

as_stated.description: The verdict exactly as the assessor worded it. null if no explicit verdict was given.

sub_claim_judgments.description: Optional. One label per sub-claim when the claim was split.

outside_knowledge_note.description: Optional. What the assessor knows from outside the source. Never changes the label.

evidence_status.description: 'locator_only' retains source references and passage locations without reproducing the passages. 'none_found_after_search' requires a search note.

search_note.description: Optional. What was searched for when no supporting passage exists.

evidence.description: Passages this assessor relied on. Must have at least one item when evidence_status is 'recorded'.

independence.description: Whether this assessment was made before seeing others. null = not recorded.

reference_eligible.description: Candidate human reference. Scoring also requires individual confirmation and resolved evidence. Always false for AI.

review_status.description: 'needs_review' = provisional, not yet approved by the record's owner.
